examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Check continuity on the closed interval and differentiability on its interior before applying MVT. It guarantees an interior point whose derivative equals the secant slope. Rolle’s theorem additionally requires equal endpoint values. The theorem is an existence result and need not identify a unique point unless the derivative is suitably monotone.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
For f(x)=x² on [1,5], what value c satisfies the mean value theorem?

**Answer: 3.** The secant slope is (25−1)/(5−1)=6. Since f′(c)=2c, solve 2c=6 to get c=3, which lies strictly in (1,5). The polynomial meets both regularity conditions.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
Applying Rolle’s theorem to |x| across zero is invalid because differentiability fails at the cusp, even though the endpoint values can match.

A corner inside the interval invalidates differentiability and may invalidate the conclusion.
